newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares post wide losses after Dow fall.
newsitem.headline: German shares post wide losses after Dow fall.

text.p: Germany's DAX index closed nearly two percent lower on Monday, unnerved by Wall Street's sharp drop on Friday amid continuing U.S. inflationary and interest rate fears.
A small mid-session rebound off the day's earlier lows never really gained ground as concern remained that the Dow Jones could be set for further falls when it reopens later on Monday.

The DAX-30 index of leading shares closed 60.15 points, 1.80 percent down at 3,279.90 after earlier hitting a day-low of 3,266.96. June DAX futures trade 31.5 points down at 3,286.0, with its day-low standing at 3,261.0.
The stronger dollar and a steady, slightly firmer Bund market lent some support but dealers said the market was nonetheless vulnerable to further losses.
"We are all looking to see how much Wall Street can salvage from (Friday's) wreckage later on -- that will be the determining factor," said one Frankfurt-based equity salesman.
The dollar traded at 1.722 marks, comfortably above the 1.72 threshold seen by many market players last week as noteworthy.
In the DAX index, dealers said that now the 3,300-point support level had been broken, there was little in the way of real support, technical or psychological, until 3,200 points.
"The market these days goes through the small-scale support levels (in between) like a knife through butter," one said.

Very few stocks managed to buck the downward trend. Auto components maker Kolbenschmidt AG firmed 1.20 marks to 29.90 after the Berlin cartel office approved a majority stake in it by the defence and engineering group Rheinmetall.
Earlier strength in drugs and chemicals group Merck KGaA, which said first quarter sales rose 12.4 percent to 1,896 million marks, later fizzled out, with the stock closing flat at 67.30.
Even the rally that car-maker Volkswagen AG has seen after last week's positive 1997 outlook statement was halted, with its shares off 22.50 marks to 1,050.0.
Newly-public mobile phone group Mobilcom was strongly lower, down nearly nine percent at 108.50 marks, cutting some of sharp gains since flotation.
Software group SAP, whose shares are often subject to large swings, lost 10.70 marks to 275.30.
